liam: quick share — ran a focused microbench comparing new-13b int8 vs fp16 under continuous batching for multi-turn chat. surprise: huge token cost reduction but p95/p99 latency tails worsen as batch size grows. rough numbers below.

liam: ```
# warm KV cache (~95% warm)
batch=1  fp16  p50=110ms  p95=320ms  p99=420ms  cost-unit=1.00
batch=1  int8  p50=125ms  p95=410ms  p99=600ms  cost-unit=0.38

batch=4  fp16  p50=240ms  p95=760ms  p99=980ms  cost-unit=0.25
batch=4  int8  p50=300ms  p95=1100ms p99=1700ms cost-unit=0.095
```

liam: notes: - int8 reduces token cost ~2.6x vs fp16 for same throughput; - latency median is close but tail balloons for batch>=4 (KV cache pressure + per-request quant dequant overhead); - cold KV runs are ~1.3x worse across the board.

tess: nice numbers. did you use continuous-batching scheduler (pack_by_token) or fixed batch windows?

liam: pack_by_token + dynamic timeout=30ms. I also tried fixed-window 50ms — tails similar but slightly worse for int8.

maria: from product/GTN POV we care about perceived slow responses (p99) and regressions in quality. do we have a small eval set (20 long chat threads) to run fidelity checks?

liam: ran a quick fidelity check: average rouge-like score delta ~0.2 pts drop for int8 on long-form, but a few prompts showed notable hallucination risk (3/20).

chad: propose hybrid routing: default -> int8 for short-turn/light prompts (<=2 turns / expected tokens < 200), fallback -> fp16 for long-form, and a canary at 5% for end-to-end GTN traffic. fallback rule should be automatic if p99 latency or quality signal breaches thresholds.

maria: suggested GTN signal set for canary gating: [p99 latency, avg token cost per completion, fidelity delta on evaluation set, user-visible error rate]. thresholds: p99 < 1.2s, fidelity delta < 0.5 pts, cost improvement >= 2x.

liam: implementation notes: put int8 behind a routing flag, start with internal 1% traffic for 24h, then 5% with rollback on quality anomalies. log full inputs for flagged prompts (PII scrubbed).

chad: rollout steps I recommend:
1) internal perf smoke (tess)
2) 1% internal canary 24h (ops)
3) 5% GTN canary 72h with evaluation watchdog (maria)
4) 10-20% gradual ramp if signals stable
